title: Fetch the postcode table once, on first use

blocks.text: The shop's checkout asks `PostcodeLookup` for the delivery region of every order. The table of regions comes from the address service, which takes a few seconds to answer and now and then times out, so the lookup fetches it on first use instead of at startup. Right after each deploy, dozens of checkout threads ask at once.

Write `table()` in `src/main/java/practice/PostcodeLookup.java`, with any fields it needs. When you're done, nothing is fetched until the first call, and the address service is asked once: every caller, including one that arrives while the fetch is still running, gets that same table. If a fetch fails, its caller gets the exception and the next call fetches again. About five lines in total.
The tests hold the first fetch open while a second checkout thread calls `table()`.

cases.says: nothing is fetched until the first call, which fetches the table once; later calls get the same table
a caller that arrives while the first fetch is still running gets the fetched table, never null
a caller that arrives while the first fetch is still running does not fetch the table a second time
when a fetch fails, the caller gets the failure and the next call fetches again

origin.section: A Double-Checked Flag Can Say Loaded Before the Value Is; a synchronized Getter Can't

concepts: With the flag set before the load, a failed load leaves it set and every later call returns null; with the value as its own flag, the next call loads again.
A double-checked flag kept beside the value can say loaded while the value is null, so a caller during the load gets null; a synchronized getter whose value is its own flag makes it wait.
